description.summary: get buffers from image capture sources

protocol.description:
This protocol enables clients to ask the compositor for a buffer that contains the contents of an image capture source. This buffer can then be attached to a surface that the client owns.
Instead of the client capturing and rendering the contents into its own buffer, this protocol moves the heavy work of rendering a captured image source to the compositor. The client requests a new foreign buffer session, gets an opaque buffer, and attaches that buffer to a surface that it owns. The compositor then fills in the contents of that buffer with the requested image. The compositor is responsible for keeping the content of that source up to date in the buffer as it changes.
The contents of the buffer are never sent to the client. Only the compositor sees the image.
The protocol relies on ext_image_capture_source_v1.
The compositor may choose to restrict this protocol to a special client launched by the compositor itself or expose it to all clients, this is compositor policy.
The key words "must", "must not", "required", "shall", "shall not", "should", "should not", "recommended", "may", and "optional" in this document are to be interpreted as described in IETF RFC 2119.
Warning! The protocol described in this file is currently in the testing phase. Backward compatible changes may be added together with the corresponding interface version bump. Backward incompatible changes can only be done by creating a new major version of the extension.

interface.name: ext_foreign_buffer_factory_v1
interface.description:
A client uses the foreign buffer factory to request a new foreign buffer session.
A foreign buffer session is created from an ext_image_capture_source_v1. This source can be backed by any source, including outputs, groups of surfaces, an individual surface, and more.

request.name: create_buffer

description.summary: create foreign buffer session for image capture source

request.description: Creates a foreign buffer session for the image capture source.

request.name: destroy
request.description:
This request should be called when the client will no longer use the ext_foreign_buffer_factory_v1.
Afterward, new foreign buffer sessions cannot be created by this factory, but existing foreign buffer sessions must remain valid up until the point of their destruction.

interface.name: ext_foreign_buffer_session_v1

description.summary: a foreign buffer session for an image capture source

interface.description:
An ext_foreign_buffer_session_v1 object is used to retrieve a opaque buffer that is backed by the contents of the image capture source that it was created with.
The image capture source is not mapped to a surface when the object is created. The client must obtain the buffer via get_buffer, attach the buffer to a surface, and commit the surface for the mapping to occur. Once mapped, the compositor keeps the buffer contents up to date without requiring the client to attach and commit again.

request.name: get_buffer

description.summary: retrieve buffer for image capture source

request.description:
Retrieve an opaque buffer backed by the image capture source that this foreign buffer session was created with.
The compositor will send a size event after a get_buffer request. This event describes the `wl_buffer` created here.
Whereas the backing store of most `wl_buffer`s must remain constant between submission and wl_buffer.release, this wl_buffer represents a compositor-internal backing storage that always contains the most current content of the source.
The compositor will send a buffer_invalidated event if the metadata provided by the `size` event following this `get_buffer` request changes (for example, if the source window has resized). When this happens this buffer will remain valid, and the content of the buffer will continue to resolve to the last content with that metadata.
Only one buffer may be active for a foreign buffer session at a time. The active buffer remains active until the client destroys it, after which a new buffer may be requested. Calling this while a buffer is already active for this foreign buffer session raises a buffer_active error.

event.name: size

description.summary: report the image capture source size

event.description:
The size event is sent by the compositor in response to a get_buffer request.
The buffer width and buffer height express the size of the image buffer in pixels, while the logical width and logical height express the size of what is being rendered in logical coordinates.
For example, the buffer may have a width of 200 and a height of 100, while the logical size has a width of 100 and a height of 50, meaning that the content has a scale of 2, as you would get by submitting a scale 2 buffer on a scale 2 output. A buffer size of 100 by 50 with the same logical size would instead mean that the content has a scale of 1, and that the compositor would scale it up by a factor of 2 on a scale 2 output.

event.name: buffer_invalidated

description.summary: sent when the client should reallocate its buffer

event.description:
The compositor must send this event to signal that the client should make the get_buffer request again.
The client should destroy any buffer that they are holding and make the get_buffer request in response to this event.
If the client does not request a new buffer, the compositor may no longer update the buffer that the client is holding.

event.name: stopped

description.summary: foreign buffer session is no longer available

event.description:
This event indicates that the foreign buffer session source has stopped and is no longer available. This can happen in a number of cases, e.g. when the underlying source is destroyed or an unrecoverable runtime error has occurred.
The `wl_buffer` remains valid with the last available content.
Calling `get_buffer` after this event will always return the same buffer.
The client should destroy the foreign buffer session after receiving this event.

request.name: destroy
request.description:
Destroys the foreign buffer session. This request can be sent at any time by the client.
This does not affect the wl_buffer objects created by this object.

entry.name: buffer_active
entry.summary: client already has an active buffer and cannot request a new one
